text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Canary cluster prompt-router-v2 (canary-7) seeing 5xx spike, error-rate 27% in last 1m. Paging oncall. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/prompt-router

deploy-bot: Deploy started: prompt-router-v2 -> canary-7 (deploy id: dply-20260317-71)

alice: seeing the 502s in logs, looks like kernel mismatch on the new endpoint. samples: `ERR::kv_cache_mismatch`

ben: confirmed 5xx and elevated latency on region-us-west-2, traces show failures at router.forward() after kernel select

carol: customers with heavy streaming (streaming=true) hitting errors. CS already filed one urgent support ticket, ticket #CS-9173

frank-sre: @dave-oncall can you take? I'm on infra for a different incident

dave-oncall: taking it. paging severity: Sev2. Quick triage: are we sure this is the canary only?

alice: yes, stable routes unaffected. traffic routed to canary-7 only. Canary share = 3% of traffic

frank-sre: logs from canary instances show repeated: `AssertionError: KV cache size mismatch: expected 65536 got 0` right before 502s

ben: looks like model runtime selects quantized kernel that doesn't support zero-length cache for streaming path (regression from runtime branch r-qtz-2)

carol: customer impact: CS reports ~120 affected requests across 3 customers (two paid, one trial). They saw immediate errors, some retried and degraded. ETA on mitigation?

alice: safest fast path: flip feature flag `ff.prompt_router_experimental` -> off for prod and canary (kill-switch). That should route traffic back to stable route.

frank-sre: agree. Initiating kill now. Command I used: 
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/ff.prompt_router_experimental/override" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"value": false, "scope": "global", "note": "emergency kill - canary 5xx spike"}'
```

incident-bot: ACTION: Feature flag ff.prompt_router_experimental set to false by frank-sre at 1719854378

deploy-bot: Canary routing updated: canary-7 traffic diverted to stable prompt-router (route-id: prompt-router-stable)

dave-oncall: monitoring - please watch error rate and p50/p95. Also check for any dangling connections/errors on long-lived streams

ben: grafana: errors dropped to 1.1% within 90s of kill. latency p95 back to baseline in 3m. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/prompt-router?from=now-15m&to=now

carol: CS: notified affected customers, created follow-up tickets and offered incident credit for impacted requests. Escalating to account teams for the two paid customers.

eve-support: drafting customer message now. Will paste in #support-updates for review

alice: root cause suspect: runtime kernel selection change in r-qtz-2. Repro steps recorded, attaching quick repro run: `curl -X POST https://canary-7.internal/prompt -d '{"streaming":true,"prompt":"test"}'` returns 502 with kv cache mismatch

frank-sre: started rollback PR for r-qtz-2 to revert kernel selection change, assigning to runtime team. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/runtime/pull/1428

dave-oncall: handoff: I'll remain on until error-rate <0.5% and no regression alerts for 30m. Oncall note: investigating potential test gaps for streaming+quantized kernels

carol: timeline note: incident started at 1719854321, kill-switch applied at 1719854378, customer impact window ~6m-18m depending on retries. Creating postmortem stub in /incidents/postmortems/pm-1719854321

frank-sre: add evals that exercise streaming + zero-length KV cache to prevent regression

ben: once rollback PR merges, let's schedule a canary redeploy with stricter health checks (fail fast on kv cache mismatch) and lowered canary share

alice: thumbs up. Will follow up with a small patch to runtime to validate KV cache before kernel select

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (feature flag off). Monitoring shows recovery. Incident severity: Sev2 -> under control.

dave-oncall: I'm oncall for the next 45m, ping me here for anything. Leaving a note to follow up with runtime and release owners. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

eve-support: customer messages sent, CS flagged top customers for follow-up.

carol: assigning postmortem owner: @alice. Please include timeline, root cause, customer impact, and action items

alice: will own postmortem, will follow up in #postmortems when draft is ready

frank-sre: closing thread for now, will re-open if we see any regressions. :white_check_mark:
